steps.title: Sauvignon Blanc
steps.body: Sauvignon Blanc covers about 80% of Marlborough's vineyards and most of New Zealand's wine exports. Marlborough Sauvignon is pungent and zesty: passion fruit, gooseberry, grapefruit, cut grass, green pepper and sometimes a sweaty, tropical edge, with very high acidity. It's almost always unoaked and bottled young.

steps.title: Pinot Noir and others
steps.body: Pinot Noir is the second grape, grown on clay-rich, cooler sites in the southern side valleys, like the Southern Valleys sub-region. It gives bright red cherry and spice, lighter than Central Otago's. Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Gewürztraminer also grow, and Marlborough makes traditional method sparkling wine from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Sauvignon leads by a long way.

steps.body: Marlborough's Southern Valleys, with more clay, are where many of its best Pinot Noirs come from.

steps.prompt: What share of Marlborough's vineyards is Sauvignon Blanc?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sauvignon Blanc is about 80%, pungent and zesty
Pinot Noir is the second grape, from cooler clay sites
Chardonnay and sparkling wine add variety
